content.title: What’s open, what’s closed in Mass. on Easter Sunday April 5, 2026?
content.text: By Chris McLaughlin | cmclaughlin@masslive.comEaster Sunday falls on April 5 this year and a number of services and major retailers either intend to stay open — some at reduced hours — or will close entirely in observation of the holiday.Many of these retailers — whom shoppers turn to almost daily for buying food, household items, toiletries, cleaning supplies and more — will largely follow in their own footsteps from past years.Since Easter is a religious holiday generally practiced in Christianity, retailers can decide whether they want to close for the day. The holiday also falls on a Sunday, so some places are closed anyway. The holiday celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ in Christian faiths. In Catholicism and in branches of Protestantism, the holiday is observed on the first Sunday following the first full moon after the spring equinox on March 21, according to Britannica.Therefore, Easter Sunday does not always fall on the same Sunday and can range between March 22 and April 25 of a given year.Here’s a list of what is open and what is closed in Massachusetts for Easter Sunday on April 5, 2026.GovernmentFederal Courts: ClosedState Courts: ClosedFederal Offices: ClosedState Offices: ClosedMunicipal Offices: ClosedRegistry of Motor Vehicles (RMV): ClosedPublic Libraries: ClosedFinanceThe New York Stock Exchange and the Dow Jones: ClosedBanks: Most banks will be closed, but most ATMs will remain open.Alcohol & CannabisLiquor Stores: OpenCannabis Dispensaries: Massachusetts regulators don’t identify specific holidays for when cannabis dispensaries must close, according to the Cannabis Control Commission. It’s up to respective dispensaries to choose whether or not to be open or closed, so check with your local dispensary.LotteryMassachusetts State Lottery: Retailers, such as shops and gas stations, that may be open can sell tickets for games such as Mass Cash and scratch tickets on holidays like Easter.Games such as Powerball and Keno continue to be played on their normal schedules despite holidays.State lottery claim centers for large prizes will be open on the holiday, meaning high-value winners won’t have to wait to claim their prizes until at least Monday, April 6.ShoppingRetail Stores: Many retail locations will remain open at normal hours, with a significant number of exceptions. Check with your local retailer if you have concerns.Aldi: ClosedAuburn Mall: ClosedBig Y: ClosedCostco: ClosedCVS: OpenHampshire Mall: ClosedHolyoke Mall: ClosedMarket Basket: ClosedNatick Mall: Open,
